chunks: And they said: "Should we believe in two men like ourselves, whose people are our subjects?"
ai.seo_question: Why did the people of Hud reject his message despite his humanity?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the arrogance of the Quraish and other Arab tribes who rejected Prophethood based on the humanity of the messengers, specifically Hud and Salih, whom they viewed as peers rather than divinely chosen guides. Their argument that 'their people were worshippers of ours' reflects a socio-political hierarchy where the elite claimed superiority over the masses, using this status to dismiss the spiritual authority of the prophets. This rejection underscores the Shia emphasis on the Imams' and Prophets' human yet elevated status, countering the notion that divine guidance requires supernatural or non-human origins.
